newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan banks may get OK to deal in property--paper.
newsitem.headline: Japan banks may get OK to deal in property--paper.

text.p: Japan's Ministry of Finance (MOF) is considering allowing banks, securities companies and insurers to enter the real-estate business, a Japanese newspaper reported on Friday.
The move would be made in one or two years after a decades-old ban on setting up holding companies is lifted, it said.
The mass-circulation financial daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun said the ministry hopes to activate the property market by allowing financial institutions to act as property brokers and rent out property.
The proposal may be submitted to parliament during a regular session starting on January 20, it quoted ministry officials as saying.
Under the new scheme, banks would be able to speed up liquidation of bad loans by renting out collateralised property, the newspaper said.
At present, trust banks are the only financial institutions allowed to act as real-estate brokers and rent out properties.

Under the proposed scheme, holding companies would own shares in a real estate subsidiary, but the plan depends on whether Japan will lift a nearly 50-year-old ban on holding companies, the paper said.
Banks and securities houses are currently allowed to set up wholly owned real estate subsidiaries, but these subsidiaries are allowed only to rent property to the parent firm, it said.
Ministry officials were not immediately available to comment on the report.
